title: English adjectives: how to use them and most common types
summary: This guide covers different kinds of English adjectives, how to use them, and examples of the most common ones. You'll want to bookmark this page!

Nouns and[verbs](https://blog.duolingo.com/verb-forms/) might be the building blocks of language, but adjectives make things way more fun! They let you describe nouns,[ask questions](https://blog.duolingo.com/all-about-english-questions/) , show ownership, and more.

## Essential English adjective topics


To use adjectives confidently in English, there are a number of topics you’ll want to study:


- [Descriptive adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/types-of-descriptive-adjectives) **.** These adjectives are great for adding detail to your speaking and writing. They can be used to describe everything from size to appearance, texture, personality, and beyond!
- [Adjective order](https://blog.duolingo.com/adjective-order) **.** When using more than one adjective in English, they need to follow a specific order. The typical order is: opinion, size, age, shape, color, origin, material, and purpose.
- [Comparatives and superlatives](https://blog.duolingo.com/adjectives-with-more-and-most) **.** The comparative and superlative forms of adjectives are used to compare things. They make it possible, for example, to tell us that your mom is taller


than your dad, but your brother is the tallest


person in your family!
- [-ed and -ing adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/how-to-use-ed-and-ing-adjectives-in-english/) **.** Adjectives ending in *-ed* and *-ing* can be tricky for English learners, but there’s one helpful rule to remember: Typically, adjectives ending in *-ing* cause a feeling, while adjectives ending in *-ed* *are* the feeling or effect.
- [Color words](https://blog.duolingo.com/words-for-colors/) **.** As you might expect, color words are adjectives that describe the color of something. They can tell us about the deep blue


of the ocean waves or the bright pink


of a flamingo’s feathers. Color words are also used in many idiomatic expressions in English.
- [Gradable and non-gradable adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/gradable-adjectives) **.** Most adjectives in English, such as boring


or cold


, are known as *gradable adjectives* . These adjectives can be described in degree (something can be a little boring


or very boring


). Other adjectives, such as amazing


or married


, are *non-gradable adjectives* . These adjectives can’t be described in degree and therefore cannot be modified with words like *a little* or *very* .
- [Demonstrative adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-demonstratives) **, also called demonstrative determiners.** These special words are helpful when you need to add emphasis or indicate exactly which noun you are talking about. English has four demonstrative adjectives: this


, that


, these


, and those


. Which demonstrative adjective you use depends on whether the noun it’s modifying is singular or plural and whether the noun is perceived as near or far.
- [Possessive adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/possessive-adjectives-in-english/) **, also called possessive determiners.** These words are used to show possession or ownership. The possessive adjectives in English are: my


, your


, his


, her


, its


, our


, and their


.
- [Interrogative adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/what-are-wh-questions/) **, also called interrogative determiners.** These are ”wh” words used to ask questions. In English, there are three interrogative adjectives: which


, what


, and whose


.
- [Numerals](https://blog.duolingo.com/numbers-in-english/) **.** There are two types of numerals in English, and they can function similarly to adjectives: cardinal and ordinal. Cardinal numbers (like one


, seventy


, and three hundred


) are used to describe quantity, while ordinal numbers (like first


, seventieth


, and three hundredth


) are used to indicate order.


Learning the[most common adjectives](https://blog.duolingo.com/adjectives-list) will make your English more expressive, so try incorporating new ones into your writing and speaking today!


## You’re so *good* with adjectives


Now that you know the basics of English adjectives, you’re ready to go out and use them all with confidence!
